input.quote: SFJ may, in its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement in its entirety at any time following a Change of Control of PB that occurs prior to the date of payment by PB of the final Approval Payment.
input.rationale: Section 15.6 already gives PB the preferred assignment freedom (affiliate and successor/M&A transfers without consent), but the bargain fails the playbook on three points, one of which is walk-away territory. Section 14.2.6 lets SFJ terminate the entire Agreement in its sole discretion following a PB Change of Control (with a 150% Development Costs payment), which is an express vendor exit right on our change of control. Section 15.6 also extends the same consent-free affiliate/successor carve-out to SFJ (so SFJ can assign without our consent), and states no reasonableness standard for consent to other assignments. Section 15.6's bar on SFJ assigning to a pharma/biotech competitor expires at Program Transfer. We therefore target the preferred position: the affiliate/successor carve-out is limited to PB, consent is subject to a reasonableness standard, the competitor bar applies at all times (waivable only in PB's sole discretion), and SFJ's change-of-control termination right and its payment machinery are removed. The fallback level is not used because it would require deleting our own no-consent affiliate carve-out. We have left SFJ's limited-partner/liquidating-trust right to assign the receipt of Approval Payments (Section 15.6, final paragraph) untouched as a financing mechanic, and PB's Change of Control Buy-Out Option (6.7.2) is a right in our favour.

proposal.summary: Limit the affiliate/successor assignment carve-out to PB, add a reasonableness standard to assignment consent, make the competitor-assignment bar permanent, and remove SFJ's termination right on a PB Change of Control.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We keep our affiliate and successor assignment freedom but limit that carve-out to PB, so SFJ may assign only with our prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld), and we extend the bar on SFJ assigning to a pharma/biotech competitor so it applies at all times. We also remove SFJ's sole-discretion right to terminate on a PB Change of Control and its associated 150% payment, since a change-of-control exit right against us is a walk-away under our playbook.

14.2.6 Termination for Change of Control of PB. PB will notify SFJ in writing promptly (and in any event within [***]) following the entering into of a definitive agreement with respect to a Change of Control of PB. SFJ may, in its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement in its entirety at any time following a Change of Control of PB that occurs prior to the date of payment by PB of the final Approval Payment. In the event that SFJ terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 14.2.6, then, in exchange for purchasing the Trial Data Package including the Research Results included therein as set forth in Section 11.1.1.4, PB will pay to SFJ within [***] of the date of termination an amount equal to one hundred fifty percent (150%) of Development Costs which were paid or incurred by SFJ.
ops.newText: 14.2.6 Change of Control of PB. PB will notify SFJ in writing promptly (and in any event within [***]) following the entering into of a definitive agreement with respect to a Change of Control of PB. SFJ shall have no right to terminate this Agreement as a result of a Change of Control of PB.
